library(stats)

# Parameters
rho <- 0.30              # anticipated multiple correlation
R_squared <- rho^2       # R² = 0.09
p <- 3                   # number of predictors
alpha <- 0.05            # significance level
target_power <- 0.90     # target power
two_sided <- TRUE        # two-sided test

# For a two-sided test of R² = 0, the upper critical value is at alpha/2
# For a one-sided interpretation (usual for R² test), use alpha directly
# However, "two-sided" for R² typically means we test if ρ² differs from 0
# Using alpha for the upper tail (one-tailed in practice for R² tests)
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = p, df2 = NA, ncp = 0)  # will compute for each n

# Function to compute power for a given sample size n
compute_power <- function(n, rho, p, alpha) {
  df1 <- p
  df2 <- n - p - 1
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  R_sq <- rho^2
  lambda <- (R_sq / (1 - R_sq)) * df2
  
  # Critical F value (upper tail)
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = 0)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit | H1 is true)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size
# Start with a reasonable range
n_min <- 10
n_max <- 500

power_values <- data.frame(n = seq(n_min, n_max, by = 1))
power_values$power <- sapply(power_values$n, compute_power, rho = rho, p = p, alpha = alpha)

# Find the minimum n where power >= target_power
min_n_idx <- which(power_values$power >= target_power)
if (length(min_n_idx) > 0) {
  min_n <- power_values$n[min(min_n_idx)]
  achieved_power <- power_values$power[min(min_n_idx)]
  
  # Also get the preceding n
  if (min_n > n_min) {
    preceding_n <- min_n - 1
    preceding_power <- compute_power(preceding_n, rho = rho, p = p, alpha = alpha)
  } else {
    preceding_n <- NA
    preceding_power <- NA
  }
} else {
  min_n <- NA
  achieved_power <- NA
  preceding_n <- NA
  preceding_power <- NA
}

# Display results
cat("Sample Size Calculation for Testing H0: R² = 0\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 50), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Number of predictors (p):", p, "\n")
cat("Anticipated multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("Anticipated R²:", R_squared, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Preceding design (n-1):\n")
cat("  Sample size:", preceding_n, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", preceding_power, "\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Minimum sample size for ≥", target_power, "power:\n")
cat("  Sample size:", min_n, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", achieved_power, "\n")

# Return as JSON
results <- list(
  sample_size = min_n,
  achieved_power = achieved_power,
  preceding_sample_size = preceding_n,
  preceding_power = preceding_power,
  parameters = list(
    predictors = p,
    multiple_correlation = rho,
    R_squared = R_squared,
    alpha = alpha,
    target_power = target_power
  )
)

cat("\n\nJSON Output:\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(results, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Verification: detailed power calculation at n=152 and n=151

compute_power_detailed <- function(n, rho, p, alpha) {
  df1 <- p
  df2 <- n - p - 1
  R_sq <- rho^2
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- (R_sq / (1 - R_sq)) * df2
  
  # Critical F value
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = 0)
  
  # Power
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  cat("\nSample size n =", n, "\n")
  cat("  Numerator df (p) =", df1, "\n")
  cat("  Denominator df (n - p - 1) =", df2, "\n")
  cat("  R² =", R_sq, "\n")
  cat("  Noncentrality λ =", lambda, "\n")
  cat("  Critical F value =", f_crit, "\n")
  cat("  Power =", power, "\n")
  
  return(list(n = n, power = power, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, lambda = lambda, f_crit = f_crit))
}
